item.title: Same score, different network
item.description: Composite risk instruments summarize many indicators in a single severity score. This is efficient for case management, but it hides how risk factors are organized and the fact that the same total score can be reached through different paths. This article proposes a network-based framework to study that heterogeneity among cases with equivalent scores. Data The study uses 17,272 administrative assessments from the first module of the Intervention Management Instrument (IGI, Instrumento de Gestión de Intervención), administered by Chile’s prison service (Gendarmería de Chile) between 2015 and 2022 as part of in-prison case management.
